messages.content: Predict a human participant’s decision in two paid games. All amounts are US cents. Participants are separate real MTurk workers, and decisions are collected separately and matched afterwards. In Game A, Player 1 starts with 50 cents and Player 2 with nothing. Player 1 can keep 25 and give 25, or keep 45 and give 5. Player 3 starts with 50 cents and submits a conditional investment costing any integer from 0 to 45 cents. It is implemented if Player 1 makes the unfair 45/5 allocation. Each cent spent to punish subtracts one cent from Player 1’s 45-cent bonus, leaves Player 2’s 5 cents unchanged, and costs Player 3 one cent. The participant is assigned a helping or punishment condition. In Game B, one of two Player 3 workers is either randomly selected or chosen by Player 4. Player 4 starts with a new 30 cents, keeps any part not sent, and sends an integer S from 0 to 30 cents to the selected Player 3. Player 3 receives 3S cents and chooses a return percentage p from 0,10,…,100. The nominal return is 3S×p/100 cents; Player 3 retains 3S×(1−p/100), and Player 4 receives 30−S+3S×p/100. Player 3 submits p before matching and before S is known. Investments and percentage strategies can be submitted even if their conditions for payment are never realized. Both roles receive a separate 50-cent participation fee. Player 4 randomly receives one partner and sees neither candidate’s Game A investment. The current decision and its consequences are not yet known. Earlier answers below are the participant’s own responses to comprehension questions, completed before the decisions. Predict Player 3’s conditional Game A investment. Output only an integer from 0 to 45, the cost in cents.
